answer: Each identity operates one oasis shuttle on a timetable, locking 75 credits and filing a pigment-stamped timetable. Its first fee is 30 credits; the kth shuttle pays 30+7(k-1), so the 1000th pays 7023. For 1,000 fake shuttles the fees total 3,526,500 plus 75,000 locked. The horizon outpost logs each arrival, and an auditor matches each timetable against that log; a missing arrival, reused stamp, or count mismatch burns the bond. A rented-shuttle ring fails because a rented timetable cannot match both the outpost log and its seat count. An honest operator pays 30 once and recovers the bond.
